chapter: Navy years and attitudes toward whites
title: End of the war and discharge in December 1945
summary: Eleven months on Okinawa, the false and real surrender, discharge on the lakefront, and meeting Emerette on the way home.

blocks.x: So how long were you in Okinawa? I was on Okinawa, I think I was on Okinawa about

11 months. 11 months. Because we secured the island completely. And then they started rebuilding. You see, and I was on Okinawa when World War II ended. And I don't know if you remember reading about the first, the false alarm, when they said the war was over, it was a false alarm. And boy, we celebrated that night. And then it was a false alarm. But the next week it was real. And everybody, all we could think of, oh boy, I'm going home. You know, glad to be alive and going home. How did you celebrate the ending of the war? Oh man, we just, we were real, shooting up in the air. And then we found it was false. And then the next week it was real. And all everybody was looking forward to was when their name would appear on the bulletin board in a draft going home. And when my name appeared by home was I'm going home. How long was it before you discharged? I was discharged December 1945. And I went in December 1942. And I can remember, see, we came all the way back and went out to the Navy base out on the lakefront. That's where I was discharged from. I can see my paper somewhere around here. But that was a joyful day. And I remember I caught the bus, all of them out there. And I got off on Jefferson Highway in Causeway. And the first young lady that I met, her name was Emerette.
